Ayon sa Section 208, 'Upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance, the President may open or close any port of entry.' Ang Commissioner naman ang mananagot sa reassignment ng personnel kapag nagsara ang isang port."},level2:{question:"Under Section 208, the power to open or close any port of entry is exercised by the President upon:",choices:{A:"The Commissioner's sole discretion",B:"The recommendation of the Secretary of Finance",C:"A resolution of Congress",D:"The recommendation of the Tariff Commission"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 208 states 'Upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance, the President may open or close any port of entry,' after which the Commissioner reassigns existing personnel subject to the Secretary's approval."},level3:{question:"What is the significance of requiring the Secretary of Finance's recommendation before the President may open or close a port of entry under Section 208?",choices:{A:"It means the President cannot act on ports at all",B:"It ensures a check by the finance authority before this significant administrative action is taken, though the ultimate decision-making power rests with the President",C:"It transfers the decision entirely to the Secretary of Finance",D:"It applies only to closing ports, not opening them"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 208 states 'Upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance, the President may open or close any port of entry,' showing the Secretary's recommendation as a required input while the President retains ultimate authority to act."},level4:{question:"The Secretary of Finance recommends the closure of a minor subport in Northern Luzon due to declining trade volume. Under Section 208, who ultimately decides whether to close this port, and what happens to affected personnel?",choices:{A:"The Secretary of Finance decides alone and personnel are automatically terminated",B:"The President makes the final decision upon the recommendation, and the Commissioner reassigns existing personnel subject to the Secretary's approval",C:"The Commissioner alone decides both the closure and reassignment without any approval needed",D:"Congress must pass a law before any port can be closed"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 208 states the President may open or close a port 'upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance,' and that upon closure, 'the existing personnel shall be reassigned by the Commissioner, subject to the approval of the Secretary of Finance.'"},level5:{question:"Under Section 208, upon whose recommendation may the President open or close any port of entry?",correct:"The Secretary of Finance",reason:"Correct answer: The Secretary of Finance. Section 208 states 'Upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance, the President may open or close any port of entry.'"}},451:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Alin sa mga sumusunod ang isa sa mga tungkulin ng District Collector ayon sa Section 210?",choices:{A:"Magpasa ng batas",B:"Prevent importation and exportation of prohibited goods",C:"Mag-supervise ng eleksyon",D:"Magtakda ng income tax rate"},correct:"B",reason:"Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 210(2), tungkulin ng District Collector na 'prevent importation and exportation of prohibited goods,' kasama ang pag-assess at pangongolekta ng duties, taxes at iba pang charges sa kanyang Customs District."},level2:{question:"Under Section 210, which of the following is a duty of the District Collector in their assigned Customs District?",choices:{A:"Enacting customs legislation",B:"Preventing importation and exportation of prohibited goods",C:"Appointing the Commissioner",D:"Setting national tariff policy"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 210(2) lists 'prevent importation and exportation of prohibited goods' among the District Collector's duties, alongside examining, classifying, and valuing goods and assessing duties and taxes."},level3:{question:"How does the scope of a District Collector's duties under Section 210 compare to the broader functions of the Bureau under Section 202?",choices:{A:"They are entirely unrelated to each other",B:"The District Collector's duties operationalize the Bureau's broader functions at the district level, such as preventing prohibited goods entry and assessing duties",C:"District Collectors have greater authority than the Bureau itself",D:"Only the Commissioner, not District Collectors, may exercise any of the Bureau's functions"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 210 duties such as 'prevent importation and exportation of prohibited goods,' 'assess and collect duties, taxes and other charges,' and 'prevent smuggling and other customs fraud' directly mirror and implement the Bureau-wide functions listed in Section 202, showing the District Collector as the district-level executor of Bureau policy."},level4:{question:"At the Port of Cagayan de Oro, a District Collector personally examines and values an imported shipment of electronics before assessing applicable duties. Under Section 210, is this within the District Collector's duties?",choices:{A:"No, only the Commissioner may examine and value goods",B:"Yes, since Section 210 includes examining, classifying, and valuing imported goods, and assessing and collecting duties, among the District Collector's duties",C:"No, valuation is exclusively a Tariff Commission function",D:"Yes, but only for shipments valued above a certain threshold"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 210(4) and (5) list 'examine, classify and value imported goods' and 'assess and collect duties, taxes and other charges on imported goods' among the District Collector's duties in their assigned Customs District."},level5:{question:"Under Section 210, which customs official has the duty to examine, classify and value imported goods within their assigned Customs District?",correct:"The District Collector",reason:"Correct answer: The District Collector. Section 210(4) lists 'examine, classify and value imported goods' among the duties of the District Collector in their assigned Customs District."}},460:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ilang oras ang ibinigay sa District Collector para i-report sa Commissioner ang designation ng acting District Collector ayon sa Section 211?",choices:{A:"12 oras",B:"24 oras",C:"48 oras",D:"72 oras"},correct:"B",reason:"Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 211, 'The District Collector shall report the designation to the Commissioner within twenty-four (24) hours after the designation.' Ito ay kapag walang Deputy District Collector at kinailangang magtalaga ng senior ranking customs officer."},level2:{question:"Under Section 211, within how many hours must the District Collector report the designation of an acting District Collector to the Commissioner?",choices:{A:"12 hours",B:"24 hours",C:"48 hours",D:"72 hours"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 211 states 'The District Collector shall report the designation to the Commissioner within twenty-four (24) hours after the designation,' applicable when a senior ranking customs officer is designated in the absence of a Deputy District Collector."},level3:{question:"Under Section 211, what is the correct order of succession when a District Collector is absent, disabled, or the position is vacant?",choices:{A:"The Commissioner immediately takes over personally",B:"The Deputy District Collector temporarily discharges the duties; if none exists, the District Collector designates a senior ranking customs officer, resolving ties by drawing of lots",C:"The most junior customs officer automatically takes over",D:"The position remains vacant until the Secretary of Finance appoints a replacement"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 211 provides that 'the Deputy District Collector shall temporarily discharge the duties of the District Collector,' and 'should there be no Deputy District Collector, the District Collector shall designate, in writing, a senior ranking customs officer,' with 'a drawing of lots' used to break ties among equally senior officers."},level4:{question:"The District Collector at the Port of Legazpi suddenly becomes incapacitated, and there is no Deputy District Collector at that port. Two customs officers have equal seniority and both are eligible for temporary designation. Under Section 211, how should this be resolved?",choices:{A:"Both officers share the position jointly",B:"A drawing of lots shall be undertaken to determine who is designated",C:"The Commissioner automatically breaks the tie",D:"The more senior officer's spouse decides"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 211 provides that 'in case there are two (2) or more senior ranking customs officers with equal length of service, a drawing of lots shall be undertaken' to determine who temporarily discharges the duties of the District Collector."},level5:{question:"Under Section 211, how is a tie resolved when two or more senior ranking customs officers have equal length of service for temporary designation as Acting District Collector?",correct:"A drawing of lots",reason:"Correct answer: A drawing of lots. Section 211 states that 'in case there are two (2) or more senior ranking customs officers with equal length of service, a drawing of lots shall be undertaken.'"}},470:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ano ang dapat gawin ng isang authorized person kapag nagsasagawa ng police authority at siya ay tinanong?",choices:{A:"Huwag sumagot",B:"I-disclose ang kanyang authority at ipakita ang written authority mula sa Commissioner",C:"Umalis agad",D:"Tumawag ng abogado bago sumagot"},correct:"B",reason:"Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 217, dapat 'disclose the nature of the authority upon being questioned at the time of exercise thereof and shall exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner.' Kailangan itong gawin para maprotektahan ang karapatan ng taong nire-regulate."},level2:{question:"Under Section 217, what must an authorized person do when questioned while exercising police authority?",choices:{A:"Remain silent until legal counsel arrives",B:"Disclose the nature of the authority and exhibit the written authority issued by the Commissioner",C:"Immediately arrest the person questioning them",D:"Refer the matter to the Secretary of Finance"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 217 requires that the authorized person 'shall disclose the nature of the authority upon being questioned at the time of exercise thereof and shall exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner.'"},level3:{question:"What is the practical purpose of the disclosure requirement under Section 217 when police authority is being exercised?",choices:{A:"To slow down customs enforcement unnecessarily",B:"To ensure the person being subjected to police authority can verify the legitimacy of the authority being exercised",C:"To allow the authorized person to avoid liability entirely",D:"It has no practical purpose; it is purely ceremonial"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 217 requires disclosure of 'the nature of the authority upon being questioned' and exhibition of 'the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner,' functioning as a safeguard so that individuals can verify that police authority is being lawfully and legitimately exercised."},level4:{question:"A customs officer conducting a search at the Port of Manila is questioned by the shipment owner about the basis of the officer's authority. The officer refuses to explain or show any documentation. Under Section 217, is this conduct proper?",choices:{A:"Yes, officers are never required to explain their authority",B:"No, because Section 217 requires disclosure of the nature of the authority and exhibition of the written authority issued by the Commissioner when questioned",C:"Yes, as long as the officer is in uniform",D:"No, but only if the shipment owner is a foreign national"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 217 requires that the authorized person 'disclose the nature of the authority upon being questioned at the time of exercise thereof and shall exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner,' making the officer's refusal improper."},level5:{question:"Under Section 217, what must an authorized person exhibit when questioned about their authority while exercising police authority?",correct:"The written authority issued by the Commissioner",reason:"Correct answer: The written authority issued by the Commissioner. Section 217 requires that the person 'shall exhibit the corresponding written authority issued by the Commissioner.'"}},472:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ayon sa Section 219, maaari bang pasukin ng taong may police authority ang isang warehouse nang walang warrant?",choices:{A:"Oo, dahil ang warehouse ay hindi principal na ginagamit bilang dwelling house",B:"Hindi, kailangan palaging may warrant",C:"Oo, pero kailangan munang humingi ng pahintulot sa court",D:"Hindi, dahil bawal ang pagpasok sa anumang building"},correct:"A",reason:"Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 219, maaaring pasukin at hanapin 'any land, enclosure, warehouse, store, building or structure not principally used as a dwelling house' nang walang warrant. Iba ito sa dwelling house na kailangan ng warrant ayon sa Section 220."},level2:{question:"Under Section 219, a person exercising police authority may enter and search which of the following without a warrant?",choices:{A:"Any structure not principally used as a dwelling house",B:"Any private residence at any time",C:"Only government buildings",D:"Only vessels docked at a port"},correct:"A",reason:"Correct answer: A. Section 219 authorizes entry into 'any land, enclosure, warehouse, store, building or structure not principally used as a dwelling house,' distinguishing this from the warrant requirement for dwelling houses under Section 220."},level3:{question:"Under Section 219, how does the CMTA treat a warehouse where a security guard resides, for purposes of the warrantless entry rule?",choices:{A:"It is always treated as a dwelling house requiring a warrant",B:"It is not considered a dwelling house under the CMTA, even if a security personnel or employee lives there",C:"It depends entirely on the discretion of the local court",D:"The CMTA does not address this situation at all"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 219 explicitly states that 'when a security personnel or any other employee lives in the warehouse, store, or any building, structure or enclosure that is used for storage of goods, it shall not be considered as a dwelling house for purposes of this Act,' allowing warrantless entry despite residential use by staff."},level4:{question:"Customs officers enter a bonded warehouse at the Port of Batangas without a warrant to inspect stored goods. A security guard who lives on-site objects, claiming the warehouse is his dwelling and requires a warrant. Under Section 219, is the warrantless entry valid?",choices:{A:"No, any residence by an employee automatically makes it a dwelling house requiring a warrant",B:"Yes, because a warehouse used for storage is not considered a dwelling house even if a security personnel lives there",C:"No, warehouses always require warrants regardless of use",D:"Yes, but only if the guard consents"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 219 explicitly provides that when 'a security personnel or any other employee lives in the warehouse, store, or any building, structure or enclosure that is used for storage of goods, it shall not be considered as a dwelling house for purposes of this Act,' validating the warrantless entry."},level5:{question:"Under Section 219, what type of structure is generally not considered a dwelling house even if a security personnel or employee lives there?",correct:"A warehouse, store, or building used for storage of goods",reason:"Correct answer: A warehouse, store, or building used for storage of goods. Section 219 states that such a structure 'shall not be considered as a dwelling house for purposes of this Act' even when a security personnel or employee resides there."}},473:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ano ang kailangan bago mahalughog ang isang dwelling house ayon sa Section 220?",choices:{A:"Verbal na pahintulot ng may-ari",B:"Warrant mula sa isang Judge ng competent court",C:"Pahintulot lamang ng Commissioner",D:"Walang kailangan, basta may reasonable suspicion"},correct:"B",reason:"Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 220, 'A dwelling house may be entered and searched only upon warrant issued by a Judge of a competent court,' kasama ang sworn application na nagpapakita ng probable cause. Mahigpit ito kumpara sa warehouse o iba pang structure."},level2:{question:"Under Section 220, a dwelling house may only be entered and searched upon:",choices:{A:"Verbal consent of any occupant",B:"A warrant issued by a Judge of a competent court based on probable cause",C:"Written authorization from the Commissioner alone",D:"Any suspicion of wrongdoing without further requirement"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 220 requires 'a warrant issued by a Judge of a competent court, the sworn application thereupon showing probable cause and particularly describing the place to be searched and the goods to be seized.'"},level3:{question:"What specific requirements must a warrant application meet before a dwelling house may be searched under Section 220?",choices:{A:"It need only state a general suspicion of wrongdoing",B:"It must show probable cause and particularly describe both the place to be searched and the goods to be seized",C:"It only needs the signature of a customs officer, without judicial involvement",D:"No specific requirements exist beyond obtaining any court order"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 220 requires 'the sworn application thereupon showing probable cause and particularly describing the place to be searched and the goods to be seized,' reflecting constitutional search warrant standards applied specifically to dwelling houses under the CMTA."},level4:{question:"Customs officers suspect that smuggled goods are hidden inside a private residence in Quezon City. They wish to search the house without first obtaining any court document, citing urgency. Under Section 220, is this search lawful?",choices:{A:"Yes, urgency always excuses the warrant requirement",B:"No, because a dwelling house may only be entered and searched upon a warrant issued by a judge based on probable cause, particularly describing the place and goods",C:"Yes, as long as the Commissioner verbally approves",D:"No, but only if the residence belongs to a foreign national"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 220 unambiguously requires that 'a dwelling house may be entered and searched only upon warrant issued by a Judge of a competent court, the sworn application thereupon showing probable cause and particularly describing the place to be searched and the goods to be seized.'"},level5:{question:"Under Section 220, what must a warrant application for searching a dwelling house particularly describe?",correct:"The place to be searched and the goods to be seized",reason:"Correct answer: The place to be searched and the goods to be seized. Section 220 requires the sworn application to show probable cause and 'particularly describing the place to be searched and the goods to be seized.'"}},474:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ayon sa Section 221, ano ang maaaring gawin ng taong may police authority sa isang barko o eroplano kung may probable violation ng CMTA?",choices:{A:"Wala, dapat kumuha muna ng warrant",B:"Maaari niyang kumpiskahin ang goods, vessel, aircraft, o bahagi nito",C:"Dapat lamang mag-ulat sa Kongreso",D:"Wala siyang karapatang maghalughog sa loob"},correct:"B",reason:"Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 221, 'In case of any probable violation of this Act, the person exercising police authority may seize the goods, vessel, aircraft, or any part thereof.' Kasama rin dito ang karapatang alisin ang false bottom o partition para mahanap ang concealed goods."},level2:{question:"Under Section 221, the authority to search a vessel or aircraft includes the power to:",choices:{A:"Only inspect visible cargo without further action",B:"Remove any false bottom, partition, bulkhead, or other obstruction to uncover concealed goods",C:"Detain the vessel indefinitely without cause",D:"Search only if the vessel is Philippine-registered"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 221 states that the power to search 'includes removal of any false bottom, partition, bulkhead, or any other obstruction for the purpose of uncovering any concealed dutiable or forfeitable goods.'"},level3:{question:"Under Section 221, when would a claim for damages arising from a search of a vessel or aircraft be valid against the person exercising police authority?",choices:{A:"Never, regardless of circumstances",B:"Only when there is gross negligence or abuse of authority in the exercise of the search",C:"Whenever any damage occurs during a search, regardless of cause",D:"Only if the vessel is a foreign-flagged vessel"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 221 states that the search proceeding 'shall not give rise to any claim for damage caused to the goods, vessel or aircraft, unless there is gross negligence or abuse of authority in the exercise thereof,' establishing a high threshold before liability attaches."},level4:{question:"During a search of a cargo vessel at the Port of Subic, customs officers remove a false bulkhead to check for concealed goods, causing minor damage to the vessel's interior panel. No negligence or abuse of authority is shown. Under Section 221, can the vessel owner successfully claim damages?",choices:{A:"Yes, any damage caused during a search is compensable",B:"No, because the proceeding does not give rise to a claim for damage unless there is gross negligence or abuse of authority",C:"Yes, but only for damage to sealed containers",D:"No, because vessel owners can never claim damages under the CMTA"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 221 states that the search proceeding 'shall not give rise to any claim for damage caused to the goods, vessel or aircraft, unless there is gross negligence or abuse of authority in the exercise thereof,' and since neither is shown here, no valid claim arises."},level5:{question:"Under Section 221, under what two conditions can a claim for damage caused during a search of a vessel or aircraft be validly raised?",correct:"Gross negligence or abuse of authority",reason:"Correct answer: Gross negligence or abuse of authority. Section 221 states the search proceeding shall not give rise to a damage claim 'unless there is gross negligence or abuse of authority in the exercise thereof.'"}},476:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ayon sa Section 223, sino ang maaaring gamitin para maghalughog sa mga babaeng traveler na galing sa ibang bansa?",choices:{A:"Kahit sinong customs officer",B:"Female inspectors",C:"Pulis lamang",D:"Hindi maaaring halughugin ang mga babae"},correct:"B",reason:"Tamang sagot: B. Ayon sa Section 223, 'Female inspectors may be employed for the examination and search of persons of their own sex,' habang iginagalang ang dignidad ng taong sinasala at dine-detain."},level2:{question:"Under Section 223, who may be employed for the examination and search of female travelers arriving from foreign countries?",choices:{A:"Any available customs officer",B:"Female inspectors",C:"Only the District Collector personally",D:"Members of the PNP exclusively"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 223 provides that 'Female inspectors may be employed for the examination and search of persons of their own sex,' while requiring that the dignity of the person searched be respected at all times."},level3:{question:"How does Section 223 balance the Bureau's authority to search travelers with respect for individual dignity?",choices:{A:"It grants unlimited search authority without any dignity safeguards",B:"It allows search and detention only upon reasonable cause, requires that dignity be respected at all times, and provides for female inspectors to search persons of their own sex",C:"It prohibits all searches of arriving travelers",D:"It applies dignity protections only to Philippine citizens, not foreigners"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 223 conditions search and detention on 'reasonable cause,' mandates that 'the dignity of the person under search and detention shall be respected at all times,' and provides that 'female inspectors may be employed for the examination and search of persons of their own sex,' balancing enforcement authority with personal dignity."},level4:{question:"A female traveler arriving at NAIA is flagged for search based on reasonable cause. The airport has only male customs officers on duty at that moment. Under Section 223, what is the proper approach?",choices:{A:"Any male officer may proceed with the search immediately",B:"The search should involve female inspectors for examining persons of the same sex, while respecting the traveler's dignity at all times",C:"The traveler cannot be searched under any circumstance",D:"The search must be postponed indefinitely until a female inspector transfers permanently to that airport"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 223 provides that 'female inspectors may be employed for the examination and search of persons of their own sex,' while also mandating that 'the dignity of the person under search and detention shall be respected at all times,' guiding proper procedure in this scenario."},level5:{question:"Under Section 223, who may be employed for the examination and search of female travelers arriving from foreign countries?",correct:"Female inspectors",reason:"Correct answer: Female inspectors. Section 223 states that 'female inspectors may be employed for the examination and search of persons of their own sex.'"}},477:{_title:"Title II – Bureau of Customs",level1:{question:"Ilang araw ang ibinigay sa isang interested party para magpakita ng ebidensya ng pagbabayad ng duties and taxes bago ma-seize ang goods, ayon sa Section 224?",choices:{A:"5 araw",B:"10 araw",C:"15 araw",D:"30 araw"},correct:"C",reason:"Tamang sagot: C. Ayon sa Section 224, 'In the event that the interested party fails to produce such evidence within fifteen (15) days, the goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings.' Parehong 15 araw din ang ibinigay para sa release ng goods kapag na-quash ang warrant of seizure."},level2:{question:"Under Section 224, within how many days must an interested party produce evidence of payment of duties and taxes before the goods may be seized?",choices:{A:"5 days",B:"10 days",C:"15 days",D:"30 days"},correct:"C",reason:"Correct answer: C. Section 224 states that 'In the event that the interested party fails to produce such evidence within fifteen (15) days, the goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings.' The same 15-day period applies to releasing goods after a warrant of seizure is quashed."},level3:{question:"Under Section 224, what happens if a warrant of seizure has already been issued but the interested party later presents authentic documents proving proper payment?",choices:{A:"The goods remain forfeited regardless of the documents presented",B:"The District Collector must cause the immediate release of the goods within 15 days from receipt of the motion to quash, subject to clearance by the Commissioner",C:"The interested party must file a new case in regular court",D:"The documents are disregarded once a warrant has been issued"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 224 provides that when subsequent documents are 'found to be authentic and in order, the District Collector shall, within fifteen (15) days from the receipt of the motion to quash or recall the warrant, cause the immediate release of the goods seized, subject to clearance by the Commissioner.'"},level4:{question:"A retailer at Divisoria is found selling imported electronics without being able to immediately produce proof of duty payment. The Commissioner's authorized officer demands evidence. Fourteen days pass with no evidence produced. Under Section 224, what is the legal consequence on day 16?",choices:{A:"Nothing happens; there is no deadline under the CMTA",B:"The goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings, since the 15-day period to produce evidence has lapsed",C:"The retailer is automatically imprisoned",D:"The goods are immediately destroyed without further process"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 224 provides that 'in the event that the interested party fails to produce such evidence within fifteen (15) days, the goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings,' though the retailer would still be given opportunity during proceedings to prove the source and payment."},level5:{question:"Under Section 224, within how many days must an interested party produce evidence of payment of duties and taxes before goods openly for sale or in storage may be seized?",correct:"15 days",reason:"Correct answer: 15 days. Section 224 states that 'in the event that the interested party fails to produce such evidence within fifteen (15) days, the goods may be seized and subjected to forfeiture proceedings.'"}},484:{_title:"Title III – Customs Jurisdiction and Customs Control",level1:{question:"Sino ang may exclusive control, direction, at management sa mga customs office, warehouse, port, airport, at wharves sa loob ng Customs District ayon sa Section 303?",choices:{A:"Ang Bureau of Customs",B:"Ang local government unit",C:"Ang Philippine Coast Guard lamang",D:"Ang pribadong port operator"},correct:"A",reason:"Tamang sagot: A. Ayon sa Section 303, ang Bureau ay may 'exclusive control, direction and management of customs offices, facilities, warehouses, ports, airports, wharves, infrastructure and other premises in the Customs Districts.' Hindi nito inaalis ang general police powers ng LGUs, Coast Guard, at iba pang law enforcement agencies."},level2:{question:"Under Section 303, the Bureau's exclusive control, direction and management over customs premises is exercised without prejudice to the general police powers of:",choices:{A:"The Department of Trade and Industry only",B:"The LGUs, the Philippine Coast Guard, and law enforcement agencies",C:"Foreign customs administrations",D:"The Tariff Commission only"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 303 states the Bureau's exclusive control over customs premises applies 'in all cases without prejudice to the general police powers of the local government units (LGUs), the Philippine Coast Guard and law enforcement agencies in the exercise of their respective functions.'"},level3:{question:"How does Section 303's grant of exclusive control over customs premises to the Bureau interact with the authority of LGUs and the Philippine Coast Guard?",choices:{A:"It completely removes any authority from LGUs and the Coast Guard over those areas",B:"The Bureau's exclusive control coexists with, and does not diminish, the general police powers of LGUs, the Coast Guard, and law enforcement agencies",C:"LGUs and the Coast Guard have superior authority over the Bureau in customs premises",D:"Only the Coast Guard retains authority, while LGU powers are suspended"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 303 grants the Bureau exclusive control over customs premises 'without prejudice to the general police powers of the local government units (LGUs), the Philippine Coast Guard and law enforcement agencies in the exercise of their respective functions,' meaning both authorities operate concurrently rather than one displacing the other."},level4:{question:"A local government unit at the Port of Cebu attempts to conduct a routine police inspection near a Bureau-controlled wharf, and the Bureau objects, claiming exclusive control under Section 303. Is the Bureau's objection valid?",choices:{A:"Yes, the Bureau's exclusive control completely bars any LGU police action in the area",B:"No, because Section 303 exclusive control is without prejudice to the general police powers of LGUs in the exercise of their functions",C:"Yes, but only if the LGU has no prior coordination",D:"No, because the Bureau has no authority over wharves at all"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 303 grants the Bureau exclusive control over customs premises but expressly states this is 'without prejudice to the general police powers of the local government units (LGUs)...in the exercise of their respective functions,' meaning the LGU's routine police inspection may proceed alongside Bureau control."},level5:{question:"Under Section 303 of the CMTA, whose general police powers are expressly preserved despite the Bureau's exclusive control over customs premises?",correct:"LGUs, the Philippine Coast Guard, and law enforcement agencies",reason:"Correct answer: LGUs, the Philippine Coast Guard, and law enforcement agencies. Section 303 states the Bureau's exclusive control is exercised 'without prejudice to the general police powers of the local government units (LGUs), the Philippine Coast Guard and law enforcement agencies in the exercise of their respective functions.'"}},485:{_title:"Title III – Customs Jurisdiction and Customs Control",level1:{question:"Sino ang may kapangyarihang mag-declare, sa pamamagitan ng executive order, na ang isang public wharf o landing place ay ilalagay sa ilalim ng jurisdiction ng Bureau para sa customs purposes?",choices:{A:"Ang Commissioner",B:"Ang Kongreso",C:"Ang Pangulo ng Pilipinas",D:"Ang Secretary of Finance"},correct:"C",reason:"Tamang sagot: C. Ayon sa Section 304, 'the President may, by executive order, declare any public wharf, landing place, infrastructure, street or land, in any port of entry under the jurisdiction of the Bureau as may be necessary, for customs purposes.' Kasama rin dito ang kapangyarihang mag-authorize ng transfer ng overstaying cargoes papunta sa inland depot."},level2:{question:"Under Section 304, the President may, by executive order, place a public wharf, landing place, or land under Bureau jurisdiction:",choices:{A:"Only upon approval of the Tariff Commission",B:"Whenever a private port operator requests it",C:"When public interest requires it, for customs purposes",D:"Only after a Congressional resolution"},correct:"C",reason:"Correct answer: C. The port operator wants authority to transfer this cargo to an inland depot. Under Section 304, who may grant this authorization?",choices:{A:"The port operator may act unilaterally without any authorization",B:"Only the Bureau of Customs may authorize this, and only through a formal request to the LGU",C:"The President, by executive order, may authorize the port or terminal operator to transfer the overstaying cargoes to an inland depot or terminal",D:"Only the Tariff Commission may issue such authorization"},correct:"C",reason:"Correct answer: C. Ayon sa Section 305, 'no person shall enter or obstruct a customs office, warehouse, port, airport, wharf, or other premises under the control of the Bureau without prior authority,' kasama na rin ang mga kalye o eskinitang kinaroroonan ng mga pasilidad na ito."},level2:{question:"Under Section 305, which areas are covered by the prohibition against unauthorized entry or obstruction of Bureau-controlled premises?",choices:{A:"Only the main customs office building",B:"Customs offices, warehouses, ports, airports, wharves, and the streets or alleys where these facilities are located",C:"Only privately owned warehouses",D:"Only areas within Metro Manila"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 305 states 'no person shall enter or obstruct a customs office, warehouse, port, airport, wharf, or other premises under the control of the Bureau without prior authority, including the streets or alleys where these facilities are located.'"},level3:{question:"Why does Section 305 extend the prohibition on unauthorized entry to include the streets or alleys where customs facilities are located, and not just the facilities themselves?",choices:{A:"To ensure comprehensive protection of the security perimeter surrounding customs operations, not just the buildings",B:"Streets and alleys are irrelevant and this is a drafting error",C:"It only applies to streets owned by the Bureau",D:"It was intended to replace, not supplement, protection of the buildings"},correct:"A",reason:"Correct answer: A. Section 305 explicitly includes 'the streets or alleys where these facilities are located' within the scope of the trespass prohibition, extending protection beyond the physical structures to the surrounding access points relevant to customs security."},level4:{question:"A group of individuals, without securing prior authority, enters an alley adjacent to a Bureau-controlled airport cargo facility at Clark to take photographs. Under Section 305, is this conduct prohibited?",choices:{A:"No, because only the interior of buildings is protected under Section 305",B:"Yes, because Section 305's prohibition on unauthorized entry extends to the streets or alleys where Bureau-controlled facilities are located",C:"No, because taking photographs is not considered 'entry' under the CMTA",D:"Yes, but only if the individuals are foreign nationals"},correct:"B",reason:"Correct answer: B. Section 305 prohibits entry or obstruction of Bureau-controlled premises 'without prior authority, including the streets or alleys where these facilities are located,' meaning the adjacent alley is covered by the restriction."},level5:{question:"Under Section 305, what CMTA term describes the unauthorized entry into or obstruction of a customs office, warehouse, port, airport, or wharf under Bureau control?",correct:"Trespass or Obstruction of Customs Premises",reason:"Correct answer: Trespass or Obstruction of Customs Premises. ## File: `./codemagic.yaml`
```yaml
workflows:
  android-apk:
    name: Android APK Build
    environment:
      node: latest
      java: 21
    scripts:
      - name: Install dependencies
        script: |
          npm install
      - name: Build React app
        script: |
          cd frontend
          npm install
          npm run build
      - name: Sync Capacitor
        script: |
          npx cap sync android
      - name: Build Android APK
        script: |
          cd android
          ./gradlew assembleDebug
          echo "--- Searching for build output ---"
          find app/build/outputs -type f 2>/dev/null || echo "outputs dir missing"
    artifacts:
      - android/app/build/outputs/**/*.apk
      - android/app/build/outputs/**/*.aab
      - android/app/build/outputs/**/output-metadata.json
```
